candidate_relations.label: Lumbar disc herniation at L5-S1
candidate_relations.reason: Lumbar disc herniation was the initial working diagnosis but was effectively excluded by MRI showing no significant nerve-root compression and the progressive bilateral/multifocal neuropathy pattern inconsistent with a single structural lesion. The reference diagnosis is EGPA, a systemic eosinophilic vasculitis causing mononeuritis multiplex in a patient with asthma history.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Structural spinal diagnosis vs. systemic vasculitic disease

candidate_relations.label: Right peroneal neuropathy
candidate_relations.reason: Right peroneal neuropathy (foot drop, failed evoked myogenic potential) is a manifestation/complication of EGPA-related mononeuritis multiplex, not the underlying diagnosis. The bilateral Achilles reflex loss and multifocal progression point to a systemic vasculitic process (EGPA) as the root cause rather than isolated peroneal neuropathy.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Peripheral nerve manifestation vs. underlying systemic vasculitic etiology

case_quality_flags: Classic EGPA presentation: asthma history + eosinophilic vasculitis causing mononeuritis multiplex with progressive foot drop
Initial misdiagnosis as lumbar disc herniation highlights diagnostic challenge; bilateral involvement and MRI negativity are key discriminators
